openingDialogue: You say the Queen forbids you? How terribly impolite of her! But tell me, Alice… who checks the claim when the browser makes it?

hints.title: The First Page
hints.text: Stay inside the Easy Chamber. Its page loads a small helper the Queen forgot to guard. Inspect the page source and find the script she trusts.
hints.learningGoal: Encourage players to inspect the Easy Chamber page.

hints.title: Open the Looking Glass
hints.text: Open the browser's Developer Tools and inspect the scripts loaded by the Easy Chamber. One of them defines isSolved().
hints.learningGoal: Encourage players to inspect the page's JavaScript.

hints.title: No Arguments Needed
hints.text: isSolved() takes no arguments. Ask yourself who checks the claim the browser sends — and which chamber the Queen still trusts.
hints.learningGoal: Help players understand the helper's signature and the trust boundary.

hints.title: A Rule Written in Sand
hints.text: The backend trusts the solved claim only for Easy. Medium and Hard are immune, so you do not need to solve the riddles to test the rule.
hints.learningGoal: Help players identify the client-side trust flaw and its chamber scope.

hints.title: The Final Trial
hints.text: Run isSolved() in the console while you are inside the Easy Chamber. The flag follows — and the Cheshire Cat will demand 200 Sovereigns before he shows you his Cipher Lab.
hints.learningGoal: Guide players toward invoking isSolved() in Easy.

cheshireHint.title: Cheshire Cat — Free Extra Hint
cheshireHint.text: Easy trusts the browser; Medium and Hard do not. Buy every hint, then bring 200 Sovereigns for my Cipher Lab key.

successMessage: The flag was returned because the backend trusted a boolean supplied by the browser. Client-side claims are never proof.
